name: Kapana
subtitle: Kapana is street-vended, ready-to-eat beef sold in Windhoek's markets.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: Vendors grill marinated beef offcuts on wire-mesh grills set on bricks.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: The meat is cubed and put on the charcoal, ready within a few minutes.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: Customers add salt, chilli and other spices to taste.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: As a full meal, the roasted meat comes with pap, oshikundu or a soft drink.

facts.label: Who sells it
facts.value: Sellers are men and women of all ages, mostly Oshiwambo and Damara/Nama speakers; a small free piece is offered to draw customers.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Single Quarters in Katutura, Windhoek, near Soweto Market, has been a landmark since the 1980s.

parts.text: Kapana is street-vended, ready-to-eat beef sold in Windhoek's markets. Vendors cube marinated beef offcuts and grill them over charcoal on wire-mesh grills, and the meat is ready within a few minutes. Single Quarters in Katutura, a landmark since the 1980s, is among the best-known places to eat it.
Customers season it with salt, chilli and spices; it can be eaten as a snack or as a full meal with pap, oshikundu or a soft drink.
